Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 33603 of 2023

Applicant :- Rajendra
Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. And 3 Others
Counsel for Applicant :- Balbir Yadav,Aishwarya Pratap Singh

Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Aditya Kumar Rai,Anjali Jaiswal
Hon'ble Sameer Jain,J.
1.

Ms. Anjali, Advocate apprised the Court today that she has filed her power on behalf of the
informant in the office of this Court but her name could not be shown in the cause list.
2. Heard Sri Aishwarya Pratap Singh, learned counsel for the applicant; Ms. Anjali, learned counsel for the informant and Sri Shatrughan Yadav, learned AGA for the State-respondent.

3. The instant application has been filed seeking release of the applicant on bail in Case Crime No.
169 of 2023, under Sections 363, 366, 376 IPC and 3/4 POCSO Act, Police Station Mahua Kheda,
District Aligarh, during pendency of the trial in the court below.
4. FIR of the present case was lodged against the applicant and according to the FIR applicant enticed away the daughter of the informant aged about 16 years.

5. Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that the entire allegations made against the applicant are totally false and baseless and actually prosecutrix is a major girl aged about 18 years and she Rajendra vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 17 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/4033163/

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: according to her own wish had gone alongwith the applicant and she also performed marriage with him and this fact is even evident from her statement recorded under sections 161 Cr.P.C.

He further submits, she changed her earlier version while recording her statement under section 164 Cr.P.C.
and in her statement recorded under section 164 Cr.P.C. she categorically stated that applicant did not commit rape with her.
6.

He further submitted that as per school record date of birth of the prosecutrix is 15.7.2007 and she was around 16 years old at the time of incident and during investigation her ossification test was not conducted.
7. He further submitted that applicant is having no criminal history and he is in jail in the present matter since 21.5.2023.

8. Per contra, learned AGA as well as learned counsel for the informant opposed the prayer for bail but both could not dispute the fact that in her statement recorded under section 164 Cr.P.C.
prosecutrix categorically stated that applicant did not commit any wrong with her.
9. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.

10. From the perusal of the statement of the prosecutrix recorded under section 161 Cr.P.C., it appears that she was a consenting party although as per school record her age was 16 years at the time of incident but in her statement recorded under section 164 Cr.P.C. she categorically stated that nothing wrong was happened against her and therefore, considering the statement of the prosecutrix record under section 164 Cr.P.C. in my view applicant is entitled to be released on bail.

11. Therefore, considering the facts and circumstances of the case, discussed above, in my view,
applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
12. Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the instant bail application is allowed.

13. Let the applicant-Rajendra, be released on bail in the aforesaid case on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall appear before the trial court on the dates fixed, unless his personal presence is exempted.
(ii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly, make inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(iii) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal and anti-social activity.
